newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain approves universal decoders in TV law.
newsitem.headline: Spain approves universal decoders in TV law.

text.p: The Spanish cabinet has approved a new satellite television regulation which will stipulate that decoders have to be compatible with different digital platforms, Development Minister Rafael Arias Salgado said on Friday.
He said the new law met European Union requirements.
Spain's first digital platform was launched on Thursday by Canal Satelite, and the decoders the group has ordered for the project will not meet these new requirements.
Arias Salgado said: "This is the (satellite) proposition under the (EU) directive and is the proposition of the (Spanish) decree, which incorporates literally the community directive."
Canal Satelite comprises communications group Prisa and Canal Plus via the Sogecable holding, as well as TV station Antena 3.

Asked if Canal Satelite would be able to continue to transmit, Arias Salgado said "Transmission rights are free and the government is deeply respectful of the freedom. The regulation that is today incorporated into the Spanish judicial regime aims...to regulate decoders so that they are compatible."
A universal decoder allows viewers to tune into not just one but all platforms available with the same equipment.

Canal Satelite will compete with the operators of the second digital platform, a group comprised of Telefonica, Radio and Television of Spain (RTVE), Mexican group Televisa and several regional television channels.
